overview: Latvia is one of the three Baltic states, between Estonia and Lithuania. Its capital, Riga, is the largest city in the Baltic states and is known for its Art Nouveau buildings. Latvia regained its independence from the Soviet Union in 1991 and joined NATO and the European Union in 2004.

geography.text: Latvia is low and gently rolling, with no mountains. About half of the country is covered by forest, and it has many lakes, bogs and rivers, the largest river being the Daugava. A long coastline of sandy beaches runs along the Baltic Sea and the Gulf of Riga.

history.text: Riga was founded by German crusaders in 1201, and the land later came under Polish, Swedish and then Russian rule. Latvia declared independence in 1918 but was occupied by the Soviet Union in 1940. In 1989 people joined hands in the Baltic Way, a human chain through Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, and independence was restored in 1991.

events.title: Riga founded
events.text: German crusaders found the city of Riga.

events.title: Russian rule
events.text: Riga and much of Latvia pass to the Russian Empire.

events.title: Soviet occupation
events.text: The Soviet Union occupies and annexes Latvia.

events.title: The Baltic Way
events.text: About two million people form a human chain across the three Baltic states.

government.text: Latvia is a parliamentary republic. The Saeima, its 100-member parliament, chooses the Prime Minister and elects the President. Latvia joined NATO and the European Union in 2004 and adopted the euro in 2014. About a quarter of its people are ethnic Russians.

economy.text: Latvia's economy relies on services, transport through its Baltic ports, and wood: forests cover more than half the country and timber is a top export. The capital, Riga, is the largest city in the three Baltic states.

culture.text: Latvians have a huge treasury of short folk songs called dainas; more than a million have been recorded. Like Estonia, Latvia holds a giant Song and Dance Festival, and its midsummer festival, Jāņi, is the biggest holiday of the year. Riga has one of the world's finest collections of Art Nouveau buildings.

items.title: Dainas
items.text: Short four-line folk songs, collected by Krišjānis Barons.

items.title: Riga's Art Nouveau
items.text: About a third of the buildings in Riga's centre are in this style.

items.title: Jāņi
items.text: Midsummer night, celebrated with bonfires, wreaths and singing.

sport.text: Ice hockey and basketball are Latvia's most popular sports. Latvia won bronze at the 2023 ice hockey world championship and, in 2024, its men won Olympic gold in 3x3 basketball. Bobsleigh and luge have also brought Latvia Olympic medals.

items.text: Bronze at the ice hockey world championship, co-hosted by Riga.

items.title: Bobsleigh
items.text: Latvia has won several Olympic medals on the ice track.

didYouKnow: Riga's Christmas tree tradition is said to date back to 1510, one of the earliest recorded.
Riga has one of the largest collections of Art Nouveau buildings in the world.

keyPeople.name: Mikhail Baryshnikov
keyPeople.text: Born in Riga in 1948; one of the greatest dancers of the 1900s.
